name: pin-shrink-hides-viz-then-library
why: Shrinking the dashboard to 60x16 used to fall back to classic and squash every panel into its window. Now unpinned panels hide, least important first: viz goes (classic has none), then the library, and the prompt stays.

name: pin-shrink-40x12-keeps-prompt
why: At 40x11 even the player doesn't fit: it hides too, and the ask panel (the only way to type a command) never does.

name: pin-grow-restores-panels
why: Growing the window back shows every panel again: hiding only sets display, nothing is remounted.

name: pin-note-says-how-to-keep-it
why: The first time panels hide, one note says which and how to keep them ('player · library hidden, window too small · pin player to keep it', cut at 40 cells).

name: pin-viz-survives-shrink
why: A pinned panel stays when the window shrinks; unpinned ones (the player, then the library) give their room up first.

name: pin-viz-shows-in-classic
why: Pinning viz shows it even in a layout that has none.

name: unpin-viz-hides-it-again
why: `unpin viz` takes it out of the setting and the layout drops it again.

name: set-pinned-applies-now
why: `set pinned viz` (the setting itself, not the command) took effect only on the next resize.

name: pin-bad-panel-name
why: A typo names the panels instead of pinning nothing or failing silently.

name: set-pinned-bad-name
why: The setting validates panel names too.

name: song-pin-drop-sound
why: `pin` is a command only with one word: 'pin drop sound' is a song search.

name: pin-resize-with-help-open
why: Resizing while a popup is open still fits the panels on the player screen underneath, and closing it shows them.

name: pin-viz-stays-above-prompt
why: A pinned viz in classic drew below the ask panel: the prompt must stay the last panel, right above the footer, in every layout but the dashboard (where ask is top right). The expected text is the prompt line, ask's bottom border, then the footer.
